# Capture inbound leads with Slack & HubSpot

**Pattern:** Lead Capture & Routing · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers capture-forms work end to end across Slack and HubSpot.

It moves through 15 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Lead Form Submission
2. Normalize Lead Payload
3. Route by Work Type
4. Process 'inbound' → HubSpot
5. Fast-Track 'outbound' + Alert
6. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
7. Merge Routed Work
8. Tag Pipeline Metadata
9. Sort Leads Newest First
10. Guard Non-Empty email
11. Save Execution Metadata
12. Align Field Names
13. Summarize Run Stats
14. Append Audit Row (HubSpot)
15. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing capture-forms work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Lead Form Submission → Normalize Lead Payload → Route by Work Type → Process 'inbound' → HubSpot → Fast-Track 'outbound' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Sort Leads Newest First → Guard Non-Empty email → Save Execution Metadata → Align Field Names → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (HubSpot) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and HubSpot aligned by hand for capture forms
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in Slack, for capture forms
- Capture forms work where "Normalize Lead Payload" is still a manual step before Slack
- Capture forms work that only reaches Slack when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Slack and HubSpot in step for capture forms, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Slack or HubSpot call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 17 nodes in this capture-forms build
- Branches rejoin before Slack, so a capture-forms run reports once rather than 17 times
- Every capture-forms run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Slack
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 17 nodes for capture forms before wiring Slack

## Before first run
Connect credentials: HubSpot private-app token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your capture forms process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.

**Do not log**
capture-forms payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
